items.summary:
ui-ux-audit. Audits a product's interface across eight dimensions, including navigation, visual consistency, responsiveness, WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility, forms, and system states. Every finding comes with a concrete recommendation.

It never fabricates search volume, rankings, or traffic. [...] Use scripts for deterministic steps. Anything that must be exact and repeatable belongs in scripts/ as code. Code runs the same way every time and executes without consuming context. The agent decides when to run it.
 Match freedom to the task. For processes that must be followed exactly, such as data pipelines, compliance checks, or migration steps, write tight, low-freedom instructions. For creative output where variety is good, leave room. [...] The description decides everything. The agent only ever sees name and description until a task matches. items.title: The Role of UX in Agentic Software Factories - NN/G
items.summary:
| Design | Designers parse the documented requirements to create, iterate on, and test designs. | AI turns an approved intent.md into a spec.md, using the company’s standards as context. The product owner mocks up and iterates on the interface with an AI-design tool, then approves the spec. |
| Build | Engineers write the code. | AI uses the spec.md to create a plan.md file outlining instructions for the AI coding agent. Once an engineer approves the plan, an agent writes the code. | [...] Product owners, engineering, and UX have long represented three balancing perspectives: business viability, technical feasibility, and user desirability, respectively. But if AI-coding agents dissolve many technical constraints and UX is reduced to context in Markdown files, then all the cards are in the product owner’s hands, and the approval gate is guarded primarily by business needs.

### Design-Stage Assumptions [...] Building an exemplary user experience is still very difficult — even with the help of AI — because it requires understanding people, not just pixels. This means we must still understand what people need to accomplish (exploratory research) and test the design to ensure it does an excellent job of delivering on that need (evaluative research). This is not the same thing as a product owner iterating a quick mockup based on a simple intent.md and passing it to a coding agent for production
